turns.content: Hello, my family car has broken down and the repairs cost too much, so I would like to replace it with a used one for less than 12 000 €. I have a 3 000 € down payment and I was thinking of financing the rest over 48 months, but I do not want to exceed 250 € per month. What is the best way to do this without straining my budget, given that I already have an existing loan?

Your project is indeed used-vehicle financing: in that case, the most suitable offer among those available is the **Expresso Auto Loan** (indicative APR of 4.99%, subject to acceptance and depending on your file).

On the feasibility of your budget:

- You have a 3 000 € down payment, which brings the financing need to around **9 000 €** (excluding any fees).
- Your existing loan represents 956 €/month, i.e. a current debt-to-income ratio of around **20%** of your income.
- Your average savings capacity is around **927 €/month**, and you have **14 695 €** of savings.

Given these indicators, a target monthly payment of **250 €** appears affordable, but it remains to be confirmed precisely: I cannot calculate the monthly payment, total cost or interest myself. The exact pricing depends on the APR applied to your file and on the term.

Two points to watch:

- Over 48 months, a lower monthly payment can also result from a longer term, which increases the total cost. The simulator will let you compare several terms.
- Your savings can, if you wish, reduce the amount borrowed (they are not required as a down payment), but make sure you keep an emergency reserve.

To obtain a personalised estimate of your monthly payment depending on the term and check that you stay under 250 €, I invite you to use the official simulator:

[URL|Simulate my car loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/credit-auto-deux-roues/credit-auto-expresso]

If you wish, I can also help you decide between a higher down payment and a shorter term.
Thank you for these details. So, if I want to stay under 250 € per month, would it be better to extend the loan term or to increase my down payment by drawing on my savings?

Both levers act on the same equation, but not in the same way.

**Extending the term** lowers the monthly payment, but increases the total cost of the loan (you pay interest for longer). It is the lever that preserves your savings: your 14 695 € remain available, which is reassuring given your existing loan at 956 €/month.

**Increasing the down payment by drawing on savings** reduces the amount borrowed, and therefore mechanically the monthly payment and the total cost. But it eats into your reserve: with a current debt-to-income ratio of around 20% and a savings capacity of around 927 €/month, your situation remains manageable, provided you do not let your emergency savings fall too low.

**My view for your case:** prioritise adjusting the term to stay within 250 €/month, and use only a moderate part of your savings as a complement if you want to shorten the term. Your 250 €/month budget looks **affordable** given your indicators (debt ratio ~20%, comfortable remaining income, available savings), but it remains to be confirmed with precise pricing.

To decide concretely between the two options, the official simulator will give you the monthly payment and the total cost depending on the term and the amount borrowed:

[URL|Simulate my car loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/credit-auto-deux-roues/credit-auto-expresso]

If you wish, tell me how much savings you would be willing to use and I will help you think through the trade-off.

Thank you, that is clearer. I think I can add 2 000 € more from my savings, so a 5 000 € down payment in total. With that, can I stay on 48 months and keep within 250 € per month, or will I still need to extend the term?

With a 5 000 € down payment, your financing need falls further, which is a step in the right direction to stay within 250 €/month over 48 months.

**My guidance: stay on 48 months.** It is the most effective lever here, because it preserves your savings (you would still have a comfortable reserve after using the 5 000 €) while easing the monthly payment thanks to the higher down payment. Extending the term beyond 48 months would only be justified if the simulator shows that 48 months still exceed your target — at the cost of a higher total cost.

**Affordability verdict:** your 250 €/month budget looks **affordable**. Your current debt-to-income ratio is around 20% (existing loan of 956 €/month), your savings capacity is around 927 €/month and you keep available savings after the down payment. The point to watch remains your emergency savings, which decrease with the down payment.

I cannot calculate the exact monthly payment or the total cost myself: the simulator will confirm whether 48 months with a 5 000 € down payment really stays under 250 €.

[URL|Simulate my car loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/credit-auto-deux-roues/credit-auto-expresso]

Please note: no compatible offer is currently available as things stand in the selection; if the simulator does not confirm your target, tell me which term or amount you would be willing to adjust.
